note: Ratchet for `scripts/reference-check.py` — the Rust and TypeScript half of the question `./gradlew :peer:structureReport` has been asking of Java. `entries` are exported symbols that nothing outside their own file names, each with the reason it is still here; `limit` caps that list and it may only go DOWN. `test_only_limit` and `local_only_limit` are the other two counters: a symbol only a test names, and a symbol only its own file names. Those are budgets rather than lists for the same reason `budget.json` counts `test_only_methods` instead of enumerating them — the population is large and what matters is that it falls.
measured: 2026-08-10 on the MERGED PR #222 review-wave tree, by running `python3 scripts/reference-check.py --json` on the merge commit and reading `symbols_inspected` and `files_searched` out of the document it prints: 2,246 exported symbols across 1,713 searched files, with a further 62 not asked because their name is in `UNIVERSAL` and 3 because they are `#[no_mangle]` ABI entry points reached by mangled name from Kotlin. Re-measured on the merge rather than taken from any one branch: a ratchet file describes exactly one tree, and taking either side of a merge silently loosens the gate. `local_only_limit` rose 90 -> 153 in this pass, and the rise is the gate getting wider, not the tree getting worse: 62 of the 63 new rows are declaration shapes the walker could not see before it learned to ask about `pub struct`, `enum`, `const`, `static`, `trait`, `type` and `pub` fields (the shape that motivated the check in the first place -- rendezvous's `circuit_idle_timeout_seconds` was a field), and the 63rd, `rendezvous/src/service.rs note_nat`, was hidden by a `#[cfg(test)]` latch that suppressed every declaration below the first test attribute in a file. Earlier stamps in this field recorded 1,735 and 1,734 searched files. 1,735 was exact for the commit that wrote it; only 1,734 was ever wrong, by one, and the allowlist-in-the-index story below explains it. A correction in a provenance field has to be right, or it costs more than the drift it fixes. `limit` stays 18 and `test_only_limit` stays 12: widening the walker flagged no new unreferenced symbol, which is the honest reading of a gate that was previously answering a narrower question than its name.

entries.why: Resolves a crate directory by name. Nothing calls it — `layout.properties` and `layout.rs` are how this tree answers that question, and this is the copy that lost.
A `.map(|(m, _)| m)` wrapper over `decode_discovery_body_with_overlay`. Every caller in the tree — `messages.rs:362` included — uses the overlay form, because the overlay is the part that matters.
Same wrapper, same overlay form at `rendezvous.rs:218`.
Same wrapper, same overlay form at `service.rs:611`.
No encoder in the tree writes an i64 through the builder. The canonical encoding has no signed 64-bit field, so this has never had a caller.
No encoder writes an unframed run of bytes; every field goes through a length prefix, which is the property the canonical encoding is built on.

Named exactly once more in the whole repository, in a doc comment a hundred lines below it at `env.rs:294`. That comment is the false-positive cause this check skips comment-only lines to defeat, and skipping it is what made the symbol visible.

One of ten bindings kept alive only by `ux-honesty.test.mjs`'s rule that every registered Tauri command has a TypeScript caller. `ipc.ts:225` says so in its own words. The command's real front end is native Compose; the desktop React app never calls it, so the rule is satisfied by a wrapper nothing calls.
Same ten. `peer_status` is announced to every configured tracker from the Android front end.
Same ten. `peer_self_test` is reached from the native diagnostics screen.
Same ten. The first-run flow is Compose on the platform that has one.
Same ten, the other half of the first-run flow.
Same ten. Battery exemption is an Android concept and has no desktop screen.
Same ten. The system folder picker is Android's; the desktop uses the Tauri dialog.
Same ten, the poll half of the picker.
